plants.name: Echeveria elegans
plants.tip: Offsets crowd the pot and hide rot at the base. Lift the clump each spring and pull the pups off.
plants.colour: Pale blue-green with translucent margins and pink tips

plants.name: Echeveria agavoides
plants.tip: The thick leaves hold weeks of water. Soak it, then leave it until the lowest leaves go soft.
plants.colour: Glossy apple-green triangular leaves with a red terminal spine

plants.name: Echeveria agavoides 'Ebony'
plants.tip: The black margin only darkens under hours of direct sun. In shade it fades to a plain green edge.
plants.colour: Green leaves with deep maroon-black margins and tip

plants.name: Echeveria agavoides 'Lipstick'
plants.tip: The red edge is a sun response, not a fixed colour. A dim windowsill gives you a green rosette.
plants.colour: Bright green with a broad scarlet margin

plants.name: Echeveria colorata
plants.tip: Water sits in the tight centre and rots it. Water at the rim of the pot, never over the rosette.
plants.colour: Silvery blue-grey with red-pink leaf tips

plants.name: Echeveria lilacina
plants.tip: The silver bloom rubs off at a touch and never grows back on that leaf. Move it by the pot.
plants.colour: Silvery lilac-grey, heavily farinose

plants.name: Echeveria laui
plants.tip: Slow, and rot is the usual end. Let the compost dry right through, and never wet the farina.
plants.colour: Thick chalky white-pink leaves under a dense bloom

plants.name: Echeveria pulvinata
plants.tip: The hairs trap water and go mouldy. Water the compost only and keep air moving round the plant.
plants.colour: Velvety pale green leaves with red-brown tips

plants.name: Echeveria pulvinata 'Ruby'
plants.tip: The red hair tips need hours of direct sun. In poor light the whole plant reverts to plain green.
plants.colour: Green leaves under crimson hairs, red at the edges

plants.name: Echeveria leucotricha
plants.tip: The white felt marks permanently if you wet it. Water at the pot rim and keep the leaves dry.
plants.colour: Olive-green leaves in white felt with russet-brown tips

plants.name: Echeveria harmsii
plants.tip: It goes leggy fast in weak light. Cut the stems back after flowering and root the tops as cuttings.
plants.colour: Green hairy leaves edged red, with orange-red bell flowers

plants.name: Echeveria setosa
plants.tip: The bristles hold droplets against the leaf and cause rot. Water underneath, never over the top.
plants.colour: Dark green rosettes covered in white bristles

plants.name: Echeveria shaviana 'Pink Frills'
plants.tip: The crimped margins catch and hold water. Keep the rosette dry and give it the brightest sill you have.
plants.colour: Grey-green with crimped, wavy pink-mauve margins

plants.name: Echeveria runyonii 'Topsy Turvy'
plants.tip: The upturned leaves funnel water into the crown. Water at the rim and tip out anything that pools.
plants.colour: Powdery silver-blue leaves curled back on themselves

plants.name: Echeveria derenbergii
plants.tip: It offsets hard and the mat traps moisture underneath. Split the clump each spring rather than letting it crowd.
plants.colour: Blue-green with a fine red line at each tip

plants.name: Echeveria pulidonis
plants.tip: The red edge is a light response. Grow it hard and dry, and do not feed it into soft green growth.
plants.colour: Chalky blue-green with a thin red edge

plants.name: Echeveria purpusorum
plants.tip: Very slow. Feed it little and repot rarely; pushing it into growth only makes the markings fade.
plants.colour: Stiff olive leaves mottled and speckled maroon

plants.name: Echeveria nodulosa
plants.tip: The red lines fade in shade and in rich compost. Grow it lean and in full sun to keep them.
plants.colour: Green with fine red lines on both faces of the leaf

plants.name: Echeveria secunda var. glauca
plants.tip: Offsets ring the parent and rot in a wet pot. Use gritty compost and split the clump yearly.
plants.colour: Blue-grey rosettes with red-tipped leaves

plants.name: Echeveria chihuahuaensis
plants.tip: The pink tips only come with hours of direct sun. In low light it stretches and goes plain grey.
plants.colour: Pale blue-grey with a pink-red point at each leaf tip

plants.name: Echeveria subsessilis
plants.tip: The pink edge depends on strong light and cool nights. It fades to grey-green in a warm dim room.
plants.colour: Blue-grey leaves rimmed pink

plants.name: Echeveria cante
plants.tip: The white farina is fragile and any damage is permanent. Never mist it, and water at the pot rim.
plants.colour: Broad chalk-white leaves with a fine pink margin

plants.name: Echeveria minima
plants.tip: Small and easily drowned. A shallow pot of gritty compost dries fast enough to keep it alive.
plants.colour: Small blue-green rosettes edged red

plants.name: Echeveria peacockii
plants.tip: The bloom rubs off wherever you touch it. Lift it by the pot and water at the rim, never overhead.
plants.colour: Silvery blue-white with red leaf tips

plants.name: Echeveria gibbiflora
plants.tip: The large thin leaves scorch behind glass in high summer. Bright light, but out of the fiercest sun.
plants.colour: Large ruffled leaves in bronze, olive and purple

plants.name: Echeveria affinis
plants.tip: The near-black colour needs strong sun. In shade it turns ordinary green and the rosette opens out.
plants.colour: Deep blackish-green, matte

plants.name: Echeveria 'Perle von Nürnberg'
plants.tip: It stretches faster than most in poor light. Give it the brightest sill, and behead it if it does.
plants.colour: Grey-lilac leaves flushed dusty pink

plants.name: Echeveria 'Black Prince'
plants.tip: The dark colour comes with sun and cool nights. A warm dim room turns it green from the centre out.
plants.colour: Dark chocolate-maroon leaves with a green centre

plants.name: Echeveria 'Lola'
plants.tip: Rot is the usual cause of death. Gritty compost, a full soak, then leave it until it is bone dry.
plants.colour: Pale opalescent cream-lilac with a pink tip

plants.name: Echeveria 'Blue Bird'
plants.tip: The blue is farina, not the leaf itself. Once rubbed off it never returns, so handle it by the pot.
plants.colour: Broad powder-blue leaves with a faint pink edge

plants.name: Echeveria 'Afterglow'
plants.tip: Big soft leaves burn behind glass. Bright light with some direct sun, and shade at midday in summer.
plants.colour: Lavender-pink powdery leaves with bright pink margins

plants.name: Echeveria 'Doris Taylor'
plants.tip: The wool holds water against the leaf. Water the compost only and keep the air round it moving.
plants.colour: Silver-green leaves in fine white wool, red at the tips

plants.name: Echeveria 'Blue Curls'
plants.tip: The ruffled margins hold water in every fold. Water at the pot rim and tip out anything that pools.
plants.colour: Large blue-green leaves with frilled pink margins

plants.name: Echeveria 'Neon Breakers'
plants.tip: The violet edge needs strong light and cool nights. Warmth and shade turn the whole rosette green.
plants.colour: Ruffled grey-green leaves with vivid violet-pink edges

plants.name: Echeveria 'Fire and Ice'
plants.tip: The red rim is a stress colour. Keep it hard, dry and bright; heavy feeding washes it straight out.
plants.colour: Pale grey-green with rosy-red margins

plants.name: Echeveria 'Violet Queen'
plants.tip: It opens out flat and floppy in weak light. Full sun keeps the rosette tight and the leaves upright.
plants.colour: Pale grey-green pointed leaves with a lilac cast

plants.name: Echeveria 'Ramillete'
plants.tip: It offsets into a mound that traps damp underneath. Pull the pups off and pot them on each spring.
plants.colour: Apple-green rosettes flushing orange and red at the edges

plants.name: Echeveria 'Raindrops'
plants.tip: The blisters only form on plants grown in strong light. Shade gives you flat, ordinary leaves.
plants.colour: Blue-green leaves with a raised blister near each tip

plants.name: Echeveria 'Purple Pearl'
plants.tip: The purple deepens with sun and cool nights. Overfeeding gives you soft green leaves instead.
plants.colour: Grey-purple leaves with pink edges

plants.name: Echeveria 'Mexican Giant'
plants.tip: Slow, and very prone to rot. Gritty compost, full sun, and long dry spells between soakings.
plants.colour: Very large chalk-white rosette with a faint blue cast
